```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.align = "center",
                      dpi = 110, dev = "png", out.width = "100%", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 6)
```

ggcalor is a grammar of cells. Every chart below is the same grid with
different cells, ordering, and tracks. The recipes are short on purpose: copy
one and swap in your data.

```{r setup}
library(ggcalor)
set.seed(42)
```

## Expression matrix with trees, splits, annotations

```{r expression, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 8}
m <- matrix(rnorm(30 * 12), 30, 12,
            dimnames = list(paste0("gene_", 1:30), paste0("sample", 1:12)))
m[1:10, 1:6] <- m[1:10, 1:6] + 2.5
m[11:20, 7:12] <- m[11:20, 7:12] - 2
samples <- data.frame(condition = rep(c("control", "treated"), each = 6),
                      batch = rep(c("b1", "b2", "b3"), 4), row.names = colnames(m))
genes <- data.frame(type = sample(c("TF", "kinase", "other"), 30, TRUE),
                    row.names = rownames(m))

ggcalor(m, cell_size = 4.5, scale = "row") +
  calor_dendro(rows = TRUE, cols = TRUE, k = 3, highlight = TRUE) +
  calor_split(rows = 3, gap = 2) +
  calor_anno(top = samples, left = genes,
             colours = list(condition = c(control = "grey70", treated = "firebrick"))) +
  calor_margin(right = "mean", bottom = "boxplot") +
  calor_legend("histogram")
```

The final order is available for reuse:

```{r order}
p <- ggcalor(m) + calor_dendro(rows = TRUE, cols = TRUE)
str(calor_order_of(p))
```

## Oncoprint

A categorical matrix gets a discrete fill. Clustering, ordering and margins
then work on presence. The memo sort orders samples so those altered in the
most frequent gene come first.

```{r oncoprint, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
genes <- c("TP53", "KRAS", "EGFR", "PIK3CA", "BRAF", "PTEN", "ALK", "MET")
samples <- sprintf("S%02d", 1:40)
mut <- matrix(NA_character_, 8, 40, dimnames = list(genes, samples))
types <- c("missense", "nonsense", "amplification", "deletion")
freq <- c(.6, .45, .3, .3, .2, .2, .1, .1)
for (g in seq_along(genes)) {
  idx <- sample(40, rbinom(1, 40, freq[g]))
  mut[g, idx] <- sample(types, length(idx), TRUE, prob = c(.5, .2, .15, .15))
}
stage <- data.frame(stage = sample(c("I", "II", "III"), 40, TRUE), row.names = samples)

ggcalor(mut, cell_size = c(3, 6), cell_gap = 0.15, border = NA, na_fill = "grey93",
        labels = "rows") +
  calor_order(rows = "sum", cols = "memo") +
  calor_margin(right = "sum", top = "sum", size = 8) +
  calor_anno(bottom = stage, size = 3) +
  labs(fill = "alteration")
```

## Correlation matrix

Order first, then mask the upper triangle. Circle area follows the absolute
correlation and masked cells are hidden with a transparent `na_fill`.

```{r correlation, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 5}
x <- matrix(rnorm(300), 50, 6, dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("v", 1:6)))
x[, 2] <- x[, 1] + rnorm(50, sd = 0.5); x[, 4] <- -x[, 3] + rnorm(50, sd = 0.7)
cm <- cor(x)
o <- hclust(dist(cm))$order
cm <- cm[o, o]

ggcalor(cm, cell_size = 9, mask = upper.tri(cm), cell_shape = "circle",
        cell_area = abs(cm), border = NA, na_fill = NA) +
  calor_text(digits = 2, size = 6) +
  labs(fill = "r")
```

## Dot plot

Fill carries one matrix and cell area another, the single-cell dot plot.

```{r dotplot, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 5}
mean_expr <- matrix(runif(60, 0, 3), 10, 6,
                    dimnames = list(paste0("gene", 1:10), paste0("cluster", 1:6)))
pct_expr <- matrix(runif(60), 10, 6)

ggcalor(mean_expr, cell_shape = "circle", cell_size = 6, cell_area = pct_expr,
        border = "grey40") +
  calor_dendro(rows = TRUE) +
  calor_order(cols = "mean") +
  labs(fill = "mean")
```

## Calendar heatmaps

Long data goes straight in. A binned fill scale and gaps give the editorial
look; `coord_radial()` turns the same grid into a ring.

```{r calendar, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
crashes <- expand.grid(month = month.abb, hour = sprintf("%02d", 0:23))
crashes$pct <- with(crashes, 10 + 25 * (as.integer(hour) < 5) +
                      8 * (as.integer(hour) > 19) + runif(nrow(crashes), 0, 10))

ggcalor(crashes, rows = "month", cols = "hour", value = "pct",
        cell_size = 5, cell_gap = 0.12, border = NA) +
  scale_fill_fermenter(palette = "BuPu", direction = 1, n.breaks = 6) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = grid::unit(10, "mm"),
        legend.key.height = grid::unit(3, "mm"),
        axis.text.x.top = element_text(angle = 0))
```

```{r radial, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 6}
ggcalor(crashes, rows = "month", cols = "hour", value = "pct",
        cell_size = 4, cell_gap = 0.12) +
  coord_radial(inner.radius = 0.3, expand = FALSE, r.axis.inside = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_fermenter(palette = "BuPu", direction = 1, n.breaks = 6)
```

## Hex cells

```{r hex, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
hx <- t(apply(matrix(rnorm(12 * 20), 12, 20), 1, cumsum))
dimnames(hx) <- list(paste0("r", 1:12), paste0("c", 1:20))

ggcalor(hx, cell_shape = "hex", cell_size = 5, cell_gap = 0.06) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Spectral")
```

## Waffle

```{r waffle, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3}
pop <- data.frame(decile = rep(c("<100", "3K", "12K", "43K"), each = 4),
                  region = rep(c("Africa", "China", "India", "Europe"), 4),
                  share = c(60, 10, 25, 5, 30, 30, 30, 10, 10, 40, 20, 30, 5, 10, 5, 80))
ggwaffle(pop, "region", "share", by = "decile", n = 100, rows = 20, cell_size = 2.5)
```

## Interactive

With ggiraph installed, cells and categorical tracks get tooltips, and
hovering a row annotation highlights the whole row.

```{r interactive, eval = FALSE}
ggcalor(m, scale = "row") +
  calor_dendro(rows = TRUE, cols = TRUE) +
  calor_anno(top = samples, left = genes) +
  calor_interactive(data_id = "row") |>
  calor_girafe()
```

## Saving

`calor_save()` computes the device size from the cells, trees and legends, so
the file holds exactly what you built.

```{r save, eval = FALSE}
calor_save(p, "heatmap.pdf")
calor_save(p, "heatmap.png", dpi = 300)
```
